title: Window.size is inaccurate on multiple monitor setup
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.5.1 and 4.6.1


### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6650 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21043.1005) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12600KF (16 threads) - 31.82 GiB memory

### Issue description

I have two monitors, one that is 1920x1080 (primary) and one that is 3840x2160 (secondary). 

When the project is launched on the primary monitor, it uses the viewport size defined in project settings, 1152x648, and `get_window().size` accurately reflects that.

When it is launched on or dragged to the secondary monitor, the window's true size (as determined by taking a screenshot of the window) is around 2020x1140, but `get_window().size` still returns 1152x648.

Similarly, when putting the window into fullscreen on the secondary monitor, the size godot returns is 2194x1234 when it should be the full 3840x2160.

This is an issue for a custom OS cursor I am trying to implement that needs to update to match window size.

### Steps to reproduce

Have two monitors of different sizes. Create a node with this script:

```
func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	print(get_window().size)
```

Note that the size does not change when dragging the window between monitors, despite the window size clearly changing.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[window-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25698732/window-test.zip)
